Term1: Diarrhea with shigella (bacillary dysentery) or enteroinvasive e. coli (eiec)
Text:
# DIARRHEA WITH SHIGELLA (BACILLARY DYSENTERY) OR ENTEROINVASIVE E. COLI (EIEC)

Shigellosis is generally a self-limited infection lasting 5-7 days. Antimicrobial resistance is common and continues to rise for all recommended antimicrobials. Treatment should be reserved for patients who are immunocompromised, or who develop severe illness.

Up-to-Date article: Shigella infection: Treatment and prevention in adults
Therapy:
## Primary treatment

Hydration and electrolyte replacement

## Antimicrobial treatment

## Inpatient

Preferred:
Ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h for 3 days [R,DI]

Alternative:
Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days [M]

For patients who are hospitalized or unable to take oral medications:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h for 5 days [M]

## Outpatient

Preferred:
Ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h for 3 days [R,DI]
Non-VA order for above

Alternative:
Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days [M]
Non-VA order for above

For patients who are hospitalized or unable to take oral medications:
Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS
